a1_rationale: A1's fit path matches its sources: the critic loss is the negated Kantorovich-Rubinstein estimate (critic.py:89, plan l.417), the gradient penalty is WGAN-GP's two-sided (||grad||-1)^2 at uniform interpolates with lambda 10 (critic.py:154-214), critics use Adam(1e-4, betas 0/0.9) with n_critic 5 and the discriminator one step (SI-01); 'none' is stock scVI (bit-identity test passes) and the unconditioned decoder never receives the batch (scvi-tools 1.4.2 FCLayers.forward zips n_cat_list with the covariates, strict=False, nn/_base_components.py:165, so the trailing label argument is ignored and n_batch = 1 adds no input; tests/scvi passes). The manifest is fair (equal backbone, epochs, batch, latent within each task) and A1 has 1,098 rows on seeds 100-102. Scoring calls scib 1.1.7's own metrics with a seeded kBET; PCR_batch for full-data fits uses the all-gene uncorrected PCA, which is what scib-pipeline does, and is identical for every A1 row of a task. prereg_rules implements PREREG sec 1-4 (84 rule tests pass). The A1-touching findings are documentation or disclosure (CR-07 pairing wording, CR-08 scib's own fallbacks, CR-09 provenance of code defaults, CR-12). Condition: the CR-01 fix must leave the full-data scoring path unchanged (do not add an HVG uns['pca'] to the prepped files), otherwise A1 must be rescored.

findings.title: PCR_batch reference differs between the full-data and subsampled scoring paths; X3 changes PCR definition between dose 0 and doses 50-100 on pancreas and sim2
findings.description: Full-data fits: the prepped file has obsm['X_pca'] but no uns['pca'] (all 8 prepped files), so scib.metrics.pcr() takes its 'recompute PCA' branch on adata.X with ALL genes; the HVG X_pca that prep_scib_task.py documents as the 'PCR reference for scoring' is never used. Subsampled fits: the scorer first runs sc.pp.pca(pre, n_comps=50, mask_var='highly_variable'), which writes uns['pca'], so scib uses an HVG-only reference. In X3, n_cells equals the full task size for pancreas and sim2, so the dose-0 latent has as many cells as the prepped file (full-data path, all-gene reference) while the depleted doses 50/80/95/100 have fewer cells and send the scorer into its subset branch (HVG reference): the PCR_batch definition, and hence B, changes inside the dose series for every arm. X8 and X3 immune_hum_mou use the HVG reference throughout, so their PCR_batch is not on the scale of X1. atac_small is unaffected (all features are training features).
findings.evidence: Check review/checks/check_pcr_reference.py on the prepped files (read-only): pcr_before pancreas: all-gene 0.482 vs HVG 0.191 (ratio 2.52); sim1: all-gene 0.521 vs HVG 0.275 (ratio 1.90); immune: all-gene 0.764 vs HVG 0.564 (ratio 1.35); sim2: all-gene 0.832 vs HVG 0.717 (ratio 1.16); atac_small: all-gene 0.124 vs HVG 0.124 (ratio 1.00). An uncorrected 10-PC HVG embedding scores PCR_batch (all-gene ref vs HVG ref) pancreas 0.559 vs 0.000; sim1 0.259 vs 0.000; immune 0.179 vs 0.000. scib-pipeline (theislab, main) scripts/metrics/Snakefile:6 passes the scenario's original file as -u and scripts/metrics/metrics.py:79 reads it without reduce_data, i.e. scIB's own reference is the all-gene uncorrected data, which is what the full-data path does. The e2e and kBET tests build prepped files with sc.pp.pca (uns['pca'] present), so the production path is untested.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the subsample branch use the full-data convention: drop the HVG sc.pp.pca call and let scib recompute the PCA on the subset's full X (or precompute that all-gene PCA with its variance explicitly for both paths). Do NOT add an HVG uns['pca'] to the prepped files: that would change A1/X1 scores and depart from scib-pipeline. Correct the prep and scorer docstrings; add a test on a prepped file without uns['pca']. Fix before any X3/X8 scoring.

findings.title: The tagged runner cannot launch the planned JHPCE filler work (X1 none/scvi_adv, X13) or score/gate X13 CPU latents
findings.description: run_stage.py selects rows by experiment and task only, and its preflight refuses the whole stage if any selected row holds a placeholder. Every X1 task block contains g1..g6 / 'A2' / 'A3' rows, and every X13 task block contains CPU rows whose adv_input 'na' unfittable() flags as a placeholder, so neither block can run before R1-R3, although PREREG sec 0 and GATE_JHPCE.md plan to run these fillers (on JHPCE) while A1-A3 are in progress. X13 CPU rows are also refused by fit_paper_config.py, and their latents (written by run_cpu_baselines.py without a 'gpu' field) fail Outputs.latent's device check, so the runner can neither score nor gate them; no other harness records their outcome.
findings.evidence: Dry runs at the tag (review/outputs/dryrun/dryrun_log.txt, --dry-run): A1 atac_small+immune+sim1 -> 1098 rows needs_fit (exit 0); X1 pancreas -> exit 4, 360 rows refused (lam g1..g6, adv_input 'A2', zstd 'A3'), so its 15 filler rows (none x 2 decoders, scvi_adv) cannot run either; X13 pancreas -> exit 4, the 16 CPU rows refused (adv_input 'na'), blocking its 35 scANVI/sysVI rows; X3 (192) / A2 (54) refused for matched placeholders, as expected. GATE_JHPCE.md (main) l.27 and l.309: fillers (X1 none/scvi_adv, X13) run in JHPCE GPU gaps.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a row filter to run_stage.py (--arms or --tags-file, recorded in the ledger) or commit derived filler manifests (rows copied verbatim, tags unchanged, SHA-256 recorded) before the JHPCE launch; route X13 CPU rows to run_cpu_baselines.py and extend the runner (or a sibling) to score and gate CPU latents (record device 'cpu' in their config, expect-device per row kind).

findings.title: X3: depletion dose is confounded with total cell count and training steps on 3 of 4 tasks

findings.title: Score rows carry no scorer provenance and the rule scripts cannot detect scores from another host or scorer commit
findings.description: Each score CSV holds tag, META, metrics, kbet_seed, kbet_r_calls and score_seconds only: no scorer git SHA, scib/scanpy/numba/pynndescent versions, host or CPU vector width. G4 showed that identical latents score differently on AVX-512 and AVX2 CPUs, so 'all scoring local' is enforced only by procedure; R1-R4 would silently accept a mixed score directory. A1's score rows have the same gap, but A1's provenance is recoverable from attempts/<tag>.jsonl (host, runner git SHA per attempt), so A1 stays valid; affects A1 as a provenance gap only.
findings.evidence: score_scib_native.py l.109 row = dict(tag=..., **META) ... l.111 kbet_seed/kbet_r_calls; prereg_rules.outcomes l.240-245 checks kbet_seed uniformity only; GATE_JHPCE.md G4 FAIL (5/12 deterministic metrics within 1e-6).
findings.suggested_fix: Write scorer git SHA + dirty flag, hostname, CPU model/flags, NUMBA_CPU_NAME and package versions into every score row; make read_scores/outcomes refuse mixed values within one rule input (as for kbet_seed).

findings.title: X13 scANVI/sysVI fits have no non-finite-loss guard: a divergence becomes an infrastructure error that stops the stage
findings.location: scripts/fit_paper_config.py:248-273 (fit_baseline uses stock SCVI/SCANVI/SysVI training plans)
findings.description: The NonFiniteLossError guard lives only in WassersteinAdversarialTrainingPlan. In fit_baseline a NaN loss either produces a NaN latent (recorded as nonfinite_latent by the runner) or a torch.distributions ValueError, which exits 1 and is retried as an infrastructure error until the stage stops (EXIT_INFRA). PREREG sec 1's 'diverged' outcome is therefore unavailable to the neural baselines (e.g. sysVI at z_distance_cycle_weight 50).
findings.evidence: fit_paper_config.py __main__ catches only NonFiniteLossError (l.287-292); fit_baseline calls vae.train / m.train on stock plans (l.258-273); run_stage.fit_done maps any other non-zero exit to 'infrastructure' (l.713-715).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Lightning callback (or a thin plan subclass) for scANVI/sysVI that applies the same per-step finiteness check and distribution-validation mapping, so their divergences are recorded as 'diverged'.

findings.title: PREREG 'Pairing' claim is inaccurate across arms: same seed gives the same init but not the same minibatch order as lambda=0
findings.location: docs/PREREG.md:31; scripts/scvi_adversarial_plan.py:235 (head created inside model.train); scvi-tools 1.4.2 dataloaders/_ann_dataloader.py:114 (RandomSampler)
findings.description: The adversary head's weight initialisation draws from torch's CPU generator after the scVI module is built and before the first epoch's RandomSampler permutation, so arms with a head (discriminator, reference, pooled, barycenter) see a different minibatch order from the 'none' fit of the same seed; MMD/Sinkhorn (no head) match. R1/R4 differences against lambda=0 are still valid (no bias; sigma is the empirical SD of the paired differences) but pair less than claimed.
findings.evidence: review/checks/check_seed_pairing_minibatch_order.py (CPU toy, seed 100, 1 epoch): generator init identical for all arms; first-epoch minibatches equal to 'none': 0/5 for barycenter, discriminator, pooled, reference; 5/5 for mmd; identical within each arm across lambda 1 and 10.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the wording in a dated PREREG amendment / Methods (shared: module init and train/validation split; minibatch order shared only within an arm). Do not change RNG handling while A1 runs.

findings.title: Silent finite fallbacks inside scib 1.1.7 enter B and C unflagged
findings.location: scib 1.1.7 metrics/trajectory.py:64-66 (RootCellError -> 0); metrics/kbet.py:152-154, 185-189 (score = 1), 255-259 (R error -> NaN per label, then nanmean l.200)
findings.description: Trajectory conservation returns 0 when no root cell is found; kBET forces a label's rejection rate to 1 when fewer than 75% of its cells are in large components or neighbours are insufficient, and drops a label (NaN) on an R error. These are finite and pass PREREG's 'required values' check, so a scorer failure can look like collapse (C) or like batch retention (B). Behaviour is scib's own, so A1 scores remain valid as scIB defines them.
findings.evidence: Installed source read in wcd-kbet (paths as in location); score_scib_native.py wraps kBET_single for seeding but records no fallback counts.
findings.suggested_fix: Record per row whether trajectory hit RootCellError and how many kBET labels were skipped or forced to 1 (wrap get_root / kBET as seed_kbet does); report these flags with R1/R4 inputs.
